mentions.quote: For the others, there is an option by choice, says Mādhava.
mentions.role: authority cited for the optionality of Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa timing

mentions.quote: In the *Bhaviṣya* in the *Parāśaramādhavīya*:
mentions.role: compiler of the Parāśaramādhavīya digest cited

mentions.quote: From this verse cited by Mādhava in the *Śivarāghavasaṃvāda*
mentions.role: authority who cited the verse prohibiting morning śrāddha

entities.description: Mādhava (Mādhavācārya) is a medieval Dharmaśāstra commentator and compiler of the Parāśaramādhavīya, frequently cited as an authority on ritual timing and optional rules.
entities.justification: Mādhava is repeatedly named as a source of rulings on Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa timing and śrāddha procedure throughout the window.

mentions.quote: Viṣṇu says: "For Śūdras, it is on the twelfth day, without mantras."
mentions.role: smṛti authority enjoining the Śūdra Sapiṇḍana rule

mentions.quote: from the previously cited verse of Viṣṇu, one should perform the sixteen *śrāddhas* in twelve days.
mentions.role: cited authority on performing sixteen śrāddhas in twelve days

entities.description: Viṣṇu is cited as a smṛti authority prescribing rules for Śūdra Sapiṇḍana timing and the condensed performance of sixteen śrāddhas.
entities.justification: The text directly attributes specific legal rulings to Viṣṇu by name in two distinct contexts within this window.

mentions.quote: since Kātyāyana has enjoined, "For all the social classes, the Sapiṇḍana is at the end of the impurity period"
mentions.role: smṛti source cited to raise a possible contradiction about Śūdra Sapiṇḍana timing

entities.description: Kātyāyana is a smṛti authority whose verse on the Sapiṇḍana rule for all social classes is invoked in a dialectical objection within the text.
entities.justification: The text explicitly names Kātyāyana as the source of the rival ruling that triggers the refutation about Śūdra Sapiṇḍana.

mentions.quote: Manu says (a. 3, ślo. 278):
mentions.role: principal smṛti authority on the superiority of the afternoon for śrāddha

mentions.quote: Thus says Manu:
mentions.role: authority whose verse connects sunset-tithi to ancestral rites

mentions.quote: Manu says (a. 3, ślo. 280):
mentions.role: authority issuing prohibitions against nocturnal and twilight śrāddha

entities.description: Manu (Manusmṛti) is the primary smṛti authority cited in this window for rules on the timing of śrāddha and pārvaṇa rites.
entities.justification: Manu is explicitly named three times with chapter and verse references, functioning as the primary legislative source for śrāddha timing.

mentions.quote: This is from the verse of Yājñavalkya.
mentions.role: smṛti authority on tithi pervasion rule for rites

mentions.quote: Vṛddha Yājñavalkya says:
mentions.role: authority distinguishing divine-rite tithi (sunrise) from ancestral-rite tithi (sunset)

mentions.quote: This is from the verse of Vṛddha Yājñavalkya and the previously cited verses
mentions.role: cited authority confirming tithi determination for ekoddiṣṭa

entities.description: Yājñavalkya and his augmented recension Vṛddha Yājñavalkya are cited as legal authorities on tithi determination for divine and ancestral rites.
entities.justification: The text names Yājñavalkya and Vṛddha Yājñavalkya as sources of distinct rulings on tithi pervasion, distinguishing divine from ancestral rites.

mentions.quote: Thus says Hārīta:
mentions.role: authority on the tithi that follows the afternoon for ancestral rites

mentions.quote: Hārīta states the time for an *ekoddiṣṭa*:
mentions.role: authority specifying temporal sequence of āmaśrāddha, ekoddiṣṭa, pārvaṇa, and vṛddhi śrāddha

entities.description: Hārīta is a smṛti authority cited for the determination of the correct tithi for ancestral rites and the temporal ordering of different types of śrāddha.
entities.justification: Hārīta is named directly as the source of two distinct rulings on śrāddha timing, in different sub-sections of this window.

mentions.quote: Gobhila says:
mentions.role: authority defining the pervasion of the evening as the criterion for a pārvaṇa tithi

mentions.quote: Gobhila states a fourfold division:
mentions.role: authority on the fourfold partition of the day

entities.description: Gobhila is a gṛhyasūtra authority cited for two rules: the evening-pervasion criterion for pārvaṇa rites and the fourfold division of the day.
entities.justification: Gobhila is explicitly named as the author of two cited rulings, one on tithi pervasion and one on the parts of the day.

mentions.quote: Baudhāyana also says:
mentions.role: authority distinguishing muhūrtas for divine versus ancestral rites

mentions.quote: the determination is from this verse of Baudhāyana.
mentions.role: authority on midday-pervasion rule for ekoddiṣṭa tithi

mentions.quote: This is from the verse of Baudhāyana.
mentions.role: authority on two-muhūrta rule for divine rites versus three-muhūrta rule for ancestral rites

entities.description: Baudhāyana is a dharmasūtra authority cited three times in this window for rules on the timing of divine and ancestral rites, including the muhūrta boundaries and tithi-pervasion criteria.
entities.justification: Baudhāyana is named explicitly three times as source of distinct rulings on rite-timing, demonstrating his authority across both pārvaṇa and ekoddiṣṭa contexts.

mentions.quote: There, Śātātapa says:
mentions.role: authority on Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa for a son who has gone abroad

mentions.quote: Śātātapa also says:
mentions.role: authority on the partition of the day for gods, men, and ancestors

mentions.quote: from the statement of Śātātapa, "and in the *muhūrta* of sunrise."
mentions.role: authority delimiting proximity of morning twilight paryudāsa to one muhūrta

mentions.quote: From the statement of Śātātapa: "The four *muhūrtas* after the *kutapa* *muhūrta*, or the five *muhūrtas*, are desired as the abode of the *svadhā*."
mentions.role: authority on the most lauded muhūrtas for a pārvaṇa rite

entities.description: Śātātapa is a smṛti authority cited four times in this window for rules ranging from Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa for expatriate sons to the temporal divisions of the day and the optimal kutapa muhūrtas.
entities.justification: Śātātapa is explicitly named four times as the source of distinct legal rulings, making him one of the most frequently cited authorities in this window.

mentions.quote: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga says:
mentions.role: authority on alternative nakṣatra-based timing when the standard Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa time has passed

entities.description: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga is a Vedic sage cited as the authority for a fallback nakṣatra-based timing rule for the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa when the primary time has elapsed.
entities.justification: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga is directly named as the source of the verse prescribing Raudra, Hasta, Rohiṇī, or Maitra nakṣatras as secondary Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa timings.

mentions.quote: a gradation of forenoons, etc., of greater and lesser measure should be inferred, says Hemādri.
mentions.role: later commentator whose view on graded forenoons is cited

mentions.quote: the statement of Śātātapa, '...even there, what is given to the ancestors with uncooked food alone is a support,' would also have a scope, says Hemādri.
mentions.role: commentator whose view on āmaśrāddha timing is cited and then refuted

mentions.quote: their mention again is for the sake of an excess of fault, says Hemādri.
mentions.role: authority on the purpose of re-mentioning solstices in piṇḍa-prohibition context

mentions.quote: since in the *Hemādri*, a *śrāddha* is enjoined on a *tithi* and a day of the week
mentions.role: digest cited as source for śrāddha-occasion specificity of piṇḍa-prohibition

entities.description: Hemādri is a major medieval Dharmaśāstra encyclopedist whose digest and opinions are cited and sometimes contested by the Vīramitrodaya author.
entities.justification: Hemādri is named four times as an authority whose positions are both adopted and challenged, revealing his central importance in the Dharmaśāstra debate.

mentions.quote: As for what is said here by Śūlapāṇi and others, that the acceptance of a *paryudāsa* is not out of fear of a *vikalpa*…that is based on ignorance of the source texts.
mentions.role: rival commentator whose position on paryudāsa is explicitly refuted

mentions.quote: And the nature of these as a *paryudāsa* is for the sake of being a subordinate element of the injunction of the new moon day…says Śūlapāṇi.
mentions.role: authority whose specific interpretation of paryudāsa is then rejected

mentions.quote: By Śūlapāṇi and others, however, this verse is written as being from the *Vāyu Purāṇa*.
mentions.role: authority who attributes a verse differently

entities.description: Śūlapāṇi is a rival Dharmaśāstra commentator whose positions on paryudāsa jurisprudence and textual attribution are repeatedly engaged and refuted by the Vīramitrodaya.
entities.justification: Śūlapāṇi is named three times as a disputant on questions of Mīmāṃsaka hermeneutics and textual attribution, serving as the primary foil in this window's dialectical argument.

mentions.quote: Vyāsa states the time of commencement:
mentions.role: authority on the kutapa as the commencement time for ekoddiṣṭa

mentions.quote: Vyāsa also says:
mentions.role: authority on the three-muhūrta fivefold division of the day

mentions.quote: from the statement of Vyāsa, "If one's own time has passed, one should perform it before the night; that is its limit,"
mentions.role: authority who re-enjoins the evening time as a secondary option for pārvaṇa

entities.description: Vyāsa is cited as a smṛti authority for the time of commencement of ekoddiṣṭa rites, the five-part division of the day, and the secondary permissibility of evening performance.
entities.justification: Vyāsa is explicitly named three times as the source of distinct rulings on ritual timing, including both the ekoddiṣṭa commencement and the emergency evening option.

mentions.quote: It is said by Vācaspati: "From the verse of the *Matsya Purāṇa*…a three-*piṇḍa* *śrāddha* should be performed even on a *saṅkrānti*, etc."
mentions.role: authority whose reading of the Matsya Purāṇa verse is engaged in the discussion of piṇḍa prohibitions

entities.description: Vācaspati is a Dharmaśāstra scholar cited for his reading of the Matsya Purāṇa verse on three-piṇḍa śrāddha at saṅkrānti occasions.
entities.justification: Vācaspati is directly named as the source of the interpretation that initiates the text's dialectical refutation of the three-piṇḍa rejoinder.

mentions.quote: For this very reason, the sūtra of Āpastamba, "Or in a commenced rite, the connection is until the completion," is in accordance with the commentary of the student
mentions.role: sūtra authority whose rule on completing commenced rites is cited

entities.description: Āpastamba is a dharmasūtra authority whose sūtra on continuing an already-commenced rite until completion is cited in the context of nocturnal śrāddha completion.
entities.justification: Āpastamba is explicitly named as the author of the sūtra supporting the argument that a commenced śrāddha may be completed the next day.

mentions.quote: Pāraskara says:
mentions.role: authority on the daivika śrāddha as performed with gods as recipients on Dvādaśī

entities.description: Pāraskara is a gṛhyasūtra authority cited for the definition and timing of the daivika śrāddha.
entities.justification: Pāraskara is directly named as the source of the verse defining daivika śrāddha and prescribing its performance on Dvādaśī.

mentions.quote: There, Kaṇva says:
mentions.role: authority defining ekoddiṣṭa and pārvaṇa śrāddha by number of recipients

entities.description: Kaṇva is a smṛti authority cited for the fundamental typological distinction between ekoddiṣṭa (one recipient) and pārvaṇa (three recipients) śrāddha.
entities.justification: Kaṇva is directly named as the source of the definitional verse distinguishing the two primary types of śrāddha.

mentions.quote: Ślokagautama states the time of completion:
mentions.role: authority on the rauhiṇa muhūrta as the time limit for ekoddiṣṭa

mentions.quote: And from the verse of Gautama.
mentions.role: authority on the tithi for ekoddiṣṭa (midday pervasion)

entities.description: Ślokagautama / Gautama is a smṛti authority cited for two rulings: the rauhiṇa muhūrta deadline for ekoddiṣṭa and the midday-pervasion criterion for tithi determination.
entities.justification: Ślokagautama and Gautama are cited as named sources for distinct rulings on ekoddiṣṭa timing within a single sub-section of this window.

mentions.quote: in the *pārvaṇa* rite, which is its modification, a regulation is remembered by Mārkaṇḍeya:
mentions.role: authority on the bright-fortnight forenoon vs. dark-fortnight afternoon rule for pārvaṇa

entities.description: Mārkaṇḍeya is a sage and Purāṇic authority cited for the rule that regulates commencement time for pārvaṇa by bright versus dark fortnight.
entities.justification: Mārkaṇḍeya is explicitly named as the authority whose verse distinguishes pārvaṇa commencement times by fortnight.

mentions.quote: by verses of Devala, etc., such as, "At the sight of Rāhu, a *saṅkrānti*, a marriage, an emergency, and a *vṛddhi* rite, they should perform bathing, giving, etc., at night"
mentions.role: authority cited to establish nocturnal śrāddha as permissible at eclipses and vṛddhi rites

entities.description: Devala is a smṛti authority whose verse permits nocturnal bathing, giving, and śrāddha at eclipses, saṅkrāntis, marriages, and vṛddhi rites.
entities.justification: Devala is named as the source of the re-enjoinment verse that makes the nightly paryudāsa applicable only to those occasions lacking a specific nocturnal enjoinment.

mentions.quote: There, Pulastya says: In the two solstices, a *śrāddha*, and in the two equinoxes, / and on all the Yugādis, except for the offering of the *piṇḍa*.
mentions.role: authority prohibiting piṇḍa-offering at solstices, equinoxes, and Yugādis

entities.description: Pulastya is a sage whose verse is cited as the primary authority prohibiting the piṇḍa-offering (though permitting śrāddha) at the two solstices, two equinoxes, and all Yugādis.
entities.justification: Pulastya is directly named as the source of the opening citation in the section on prohibited piṇḍa-offering times.

mentions.quote: Bṛhatparāśara says: And in Bharaṇī, one should not perform the offering of the *piṇḍa*.
mentions.role: authority prohibiting piṇḍa-offering on the Bharaṇī nakṣatra

entities.description: Bṛhatparāśara is a smṛti authority cited for the prohibition of piṇḍa-offering during the Bharaṇī nakṣatra in the Mahālaya fortnight.
entities.justification: Bṛhatparāśara is directly named as the source of the piṇḍa prohibition on Bharaṇī.

mentions.quote: Kārṣṇājini says: In a marriage, a vow, and a tonsure ceremony, for a year, half a year, and half of that, / one should not perform the offering of the *piṇḍa*
mentions.role: authority imposing graduated piṇḍa prohibitions after life-cycle events

entities.description: Kārṣṇājini is a smṛti authority who specifies graded periods of piṇḍa prohibition following marriage, vow, and tonsure ceremonies.
entities.justification: Kārṣṇājini is directly named as the source of the tiered piṇḍa-prohibition periods after saṃskāra events.

mentions.quote: Jyotiḥparāśara says: When a marriage has been performed, the *sapiṇḍas* should avoid for twelve months the offering of the *piṇḍa*; in a sacred thread ceremony, for six months.
mentions.role: authority extending piṇḍa prohibition to sapiṇḍa relatives after marriage and upanayana

entities.description: Jyotiḥparāśara is an astrological or smṛti authority who extends the piṇḍa-prohibition to sapiṇḍa relatives for twelve months after marriage and six months after upanayana.
entities.justification: Jyotiḥparāśara is directly named as the source of the rule extending piṇḍa prohibitions to sapiṇḍa relatives.

mentions.quote: the determination is from this verse of Vyāghra.
mentions.role: authority on the kharva/darpa/hiṃsā tripartite typology of tithi for pārvaṇa timing

entities.description: Vyāghra is a smṛti authority cited for the threefold typology of tithi (kharva/equal, darpa/increasing, hiṃsā/decreasing) used to decide which day to perform pārvaṇa when equal afternoon pervasion occurs.
entities.justification: Vyāghra is directly named as the source of the decisive verse on kharva, darpa, and hiṃsā tithi-types.

mentions.quote: a *daivaśrāddha* is stated by Viśvāmitra, beginning with, "The *śrāddha* that is with the gods as the recipient, that is called *daivika*."
mentions.role: authority who formally defines daivika śrāddha

entities.description: Viśvāmitra is cited as the authority who formally defines daivika śrāddha as that which has gods as its recipient.
entities.justification: Viśvāmitra is directly named as the definer of daivika śrāddha, providing the textual basis for its discussion in this window.

mentions.quote: From the statement of Vyāghrapāda: "The *tithi* which is for three *muhūrtas* after the morning time, or a *tithi* of two *muhūrtas*, one should perform an *āmaśrāddha* there."
mentions.role: authority specifying the muhūrta threshold for āmaśrāddha tithi

entities.description: Vyāghrapāda is a smṛti authority cited for the specific muhūrta-based tithi criterion for performing an āmaśrāddha.
entities.justification: Vyāghrapāda is directly named as the source of the ruling on the minimum tithi duration for āmaśrāddha performance.

mentions.quote: For Śūdras, however, the Sapiṇḍana is on the twelfth day.
mentions.role: social group for whom a special Sapiṇḍana timing rule applies

mentions.quote: Viṣṇu says: "For Śūdras, it is on the twelfth day, without mantras."
mentions.role: social group whose Sapiṇḍana is mantra-less and on the twelfth day

mentions.quote: this injunction of the forenoon in an *āmaśrāddha* applies only to an *āmaśrāddha* performed by a twice-born, not to an *āmaśrāddha* performed by a Śūdra.
mentions.role: social group subject to differentiated āmaśrāddha timing rule

entities.description: Śūdras are the fourth social class for whom Dharmaśāstra prescribes differentiated rules on Sapiṇḍana timing (twelfth day, mantra-free) and āmaśrāddha performance.
entities.justification: Śūdras are named as the specific group whose ritual obligations differ from those of twice-born classes in multiple sub-sections of this window.

mentions.quote: At the sight of Rāhu, a *saṅkrānti*, a marriage, an emergency, and a *vṛddhi* rite, they should perform bathing, giving, etc., at night
mentions.role: mythological cause of eclipse (Rāhu-sighting) that triggers nocturnal śrāddha permission

entities.description: Rāhu is the eclipsing demon whose sighting (i.e., an eclipse) is cited as one of the occasions that permits nocturnal śrāddha and bathing.
entities.justification: Rāhu is named as the trigger-event for the nocturnal permission in the verse of Devala, connecting the mythological eclipse-cause to śrāddha jurisprudence.

mentions.quote: only a Sapiṇḍana performed at the primary time is the cause of the release from the state of a ghost
mentions.role: ritual event whose correct timing determines efficacy

mentions.quote: The Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa is when the year is complete, or on an auspicious occasion, / on the twelfth day, in the view of some, and on the eleventh likewise.
mentions.role: ritual event whose permissible timings are enumerated

mentions.quote: Thus ends the time for the Sapiṇḍana.
mentions.role: formal section-end marker confirming the event as the topic of this sub-section

entities.description: The Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa (or Sapiṇḍana) is the ancestral rite that incorporates the recently deceased into the piṇḍa lineage of ancestors; this window extensively debates its correct primary and secondary timing.
entities.justification: The Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa is the central ritual event under discussion in the opening portion of this window, with multiple paragraphs devoted to its timing.

mentions.quote: He by whom a *śrāddha* is performed on it becomes one who has performed the Gayā *śrāddha*.
mentions.role: sacred site invoked as the standard of merit for Bharaṇī śrāddha

mentions.quote: the offering of the *piṇḍa* in the Gaṅgā is rare in the three worlds
mentions.role: sacred site mentioned in restriction context

entities.description: Gayā is the preeminent sacred site for śrāddha rites, invoked as the measure of merit against which Bharaṇī-nakṣatra śrāddha is compared.
entities.justification: Gayā is named as the gold-standard of śrāddha merit in the Matsya Purāṇa verse cited within the piṇḍa-prohibition discussion.

mentions.quote: the offering of the *piṇḍa* in the Gaṅgā is rare in the three worlds
mentions.role: sacred river as the locus of the exceptional piṇḍa-offering restriction from Brahmavaivarta

entities.description: The Gaṅgā is the sacred river cited as the specific locus for the Brahmavaivarta verse restricting piṇḍa-offering during eclipse in Capricorn.
entities.justification: The Gaṅgā is named in the cited verse as the place where the exceptional eclipse-Capricorn piṇḍa restriction applies.

mentions.quote: Deity of the ancestors = Maghā.
mentions.role: nakṣatra identified as the deity of the ancestors in the Devī Purāṇa context

mentions.quote: On Nandā, Aśvinī, Kāma, Sunday, Tuesday, Bhṛgu, Agni, Pitṛ, and the *nakṣatra* of Kāla
mentions.role: nakṣatra in a list of inauspicious piṇḍa-offering times for Mahālaya

entities.description: Maghā is a nakṣatra identified as the presiding deity of the ancestors and cited as a day on which the piṇḍa offering is prohibited in certain śrāddha contexts.
entities.justification: Maghā is named both as a deity of ancestors (Devī Purāṇa) and as an inauspicious tithi for piṇḍa in the Prayogapārijāta list.

mentions.quote: Bṛhatparāśara says: And in Bharaṇī, one should not perform the offering of the *piṇḍa*.
mentions.role: nakṣatra during which piṇḍa-offering is prohibited in Mahālaya śrāddha

mentions.quote: Bharaṇī in the fortnight of the ancestors is declared to be great.
mentions.role: nakṣatra praised as auspicious for śrāddha in the Mahālaya period

entities.description: Bharaṇī is a nakṣatra that is simultaneously praised as auspicious for śrāddha performance during Mahālaya and subject to a specific prohibition of piṇḍa-offering within it.
entities.justification: Bharaṇī is named in both a permissive and a prohibitive context, revealing the text's effort to reconcile conflicting smṛti rulings.

mentions.quote: Now, the *kutapa* time.
mentions.role: technical temporal concept whose definition is the subject of the sub-section

mentions.quote: And that is the eighth *muhūrta* of the day.
mentions.role: kutapa identified as the eighth of the fifteen daily muhūrtas

mentions.quote: the five *muhūrtas* beginning with the *kutapa* are most praised in a *pārvaṇa* rite.
mentions.role: kutapa as the start of the most auspicious window for pārvaṇa

entities.description: The kutapa is the eighth of fifteen daily muhūrtas, occurring at solar zenith, regarded as the most auspicious time for ancestral rites because its heat penetrates the earth completely.
entities.justification: The kutapa is formally defined and repeatedly cited as the optimal commencement time for pārvaṇa and ekoddiṣṭa śrāddhas across multiple sub-sections of this window.

mentions.quote: Therefore, these are only prohibitive exceptions (*paryudāsa*).
mentions.role: Mīmāṃsā hermeneutic category applied to the śrāddha timing prohibitions

mentions.quote: As for what is said here by Śūlapāṇi and others, that the acceptance of a *paryudāsa* is not out of fear of a *vikalpa*…that is based on ignorance of the source texts.
mentions.role: contested hermeneutic category at the center of the rival-commentator debate

mentions.quote: Therefore, the *paryudāsa* is only by the restriction of the civil day
mentions.role: resolution of the paryudāsa debate: restriction is of the civil day, not the lunar tithi

entities.description: Paryudāsa is a Mīmāṃsā hermeneutic concept denoting a prohibitive exception that limits (rather than negates) an injunction; the window debates whether the night-prohibition on śrāddha is a paryudāsa or a pratiṣedha.
entities.justification: The entire central dialectical section of this window turns on the correct classification of the nocturnal prohibition as a paryudāsa versus a pratiṣedha, engaging Śūlapāṇi's view and the text's refutation.

mentions.quote: And these are not simple prohibitions (*pratiṣedha*), because it would lead to the undesirable consequence of an option (*vikalpa*).
mentions.role: Mīmāṃsā hermeneutic category rejected for the śrāddha timing prohibitions

entities.description: Pratiṣedha is the Mīmāṃsā category of a simple, outright prohibition; the text argues that the nocturnal śrāddha prohibition cannot be a pratiṣedha because doing so would generate an unwanted optionality.
entities.justification: Pratiṣedha is introduced and rejected as a category in the hermeneutic argument about the nature of the night and twilight prohibitions.

themes.topic: Timing of the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite: primary vs. secondary occasions

mentions.quote: only a Sapiṇḍana performed at the primary time is the cause of the release from the state of a ghost
the end of the year is primary; the eleventh month, which is proximate to it, is secondary
Thus ends the time for the Sapiṇḍana.

themes.justification: The opening section of this window systematically enumerates and debates which dates constitute primary versus secondary occasions for the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, citing multiple smṛtis.

themes.topic: Tithi determination for pārvaṇa śrāddha by afternoon (aparāhṇa) pervasion

mentions.quote: if the *tithi* on which a *pārvaṇa* *śrāddha* is enjoined falls on two days, then on whichever day…it pervades the afternoon, on that day the *pārvaṇa* should be performed
When it pervades a part of the afternoon on two days unequally, then the one with the greater pervasion should be taken

themes.justification: The determination of tithi by afternoon pervasion is the central technical problem of the pārvaṇa sub-section, addressed through cascading rules for equal, unequal, and absent pervasion.

themes.topic: Fivefold and fourfold divisions of the day and the hierarchy of their parts

mentions.quote: there are five parts, named morning (*prātaḥ*), late morning (*saṅgava*), midday (*madhyāhna*), afternoon (*aparāhṇa*), and evening (*sāyāhna*)
Gobhila states a fourfold division: The forenoon is a *prahara* and a half; midday is a *prahara* likewise. / The afternoon is from the third; and the evening is after that.

themes.justification: This window devotes an entire named sub-section ('Divisions of the Day') to reconciling the twofold, threefold, fourfold, fivefold, and fifteenfold muhūrta divisions of the day across multiple smṛtis.

themes.topic: Mīmāṃsā hermeneutics applied to śrāddha prohibitions: paryudāsa vs. pratiṣedha

mentions.quote: And these are not simple prohibitions (*pratiṣedha*), because it would lead to the undesirable consequence of an option (*vikalpa*).
Therefore, these are only prohibitive exceptions (*paryudāsa*).
As for what is said here by Śūlapāṇi and others…that is based on ignorance of the source texts.

themes.justification: The longest dialectical section in this window is dedicated to the Mīmāṃsā classification of the nocturnal and twilight prohibitions, drawing on vikalpa, paryudāsa, pratiṣedha, and utkarṣa concepts.

themes.topic: Differential application of śrāddha rules by varṇa (caste status)

mentions.quote: For Śūdras, however, the Sapiṇḍana is on the twelfth day.
this injunction of the forenoon in an *āmaśrāddha* applies only to an *āmaśrāddha* performed by a twice-born, not to an *āmaśrāddha* performed by a Śūdra.

themes.justification: Multiple sub-sections specify divergent rules for Śūdras versus twice-born classes regarding Sapiṇḍana timing, mantra use, and āmaśrāddha timing, making varṇa-differential application a recurring implicit organising principle.

themes.topic: Prohibited times for piṇḍa-offering: nakṣatras, tithis, weekdays, and life-cycle events

mentions.quote: In the two solstices, a *śrāddha*, and in the two equinoxes, / and on all the Yugādis, except for the offering of the *piṇḍa*.
Bṛhatparāśara says: And in Bharaṇī, one should not perform the offering of the *piṇḍa*.
In a marriage, a vow, and a tonsure ceremony, for a year, half a year, and half of that, / one should not perform the offering of the *piṇḍa*

themes.justification: The final section of this window systematically catalogues piṇḍa prohibitions across Yugādis, saṅkrāntis, individual nakṣatras, weekdays, tithis, and post-saṃskāra periods, with the Vīramitrodaya adjudicating between conflicting smṛtis.

themes.topic: Conflict reconciliation among smṛti authorities on ritual timing

mentions.quote: In reality, however, the prohibition is justified by the difference of sages.
That is incorrect.
Others, however, explain these verses as they are heard.

themes.justification: Throughout the window the Vīramitrodaya explicitly adjudicates between rival smṛti opinions using formulae such as 'In reality…', 'That is incorrect', and 'the difference of sages', implying a systematic harmonization program even where not foregrounded.

citations.justification: The Caturviṃśatimata is quoted as an authority for the enumeration of primary Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa times including completion of the year, auspicious occasions, the twelfth day, and the eleventh day.
The Bhaviṣya section of the Parāśaramādhavīya is cited for the rule that a fire-less sacrificer should perform Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa for a fire-less deceased at year-end or alternative times.

citations.quote: another time is stated in the *Mādhavīya*—
citations.justification: The Mādhavīya is cited as the source for Ṛṣyaśṛṅga's verse providing fallback nakṣatra-based timing for a missed Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa.
Manusmṛti 3.278 is cited as authority for the superiority of the afternoon over the forenoon in a śrāddha.
A second verse of Manu is cited to establish that the tithi connected with the afternoon and on which the sun sets is the ancestral tithi.
Manusmṛti 3.280 is cited as the primary authority for the prohibition of nocturnal and twilight śrāddha.

citations.quote: Whichever rite has whichever time, the *tithi* pervading that time / should be used for those rites; decrease and increase are not the cause.
citations.justification: A verse of Yājñavalkya is cited as the definitive authority for the tithi-pervasion principle applied to śrāddha rites.
Vṛddha Yājñavalkya is cited for the rule distinguishing the sunrise-tithi for divine rites from the sunset-tithi for ancestral rites.
The Śivarahasya is cited jointly with the Saurapurāṇa for the rule that the end of the tithi should be observed for divine rites and the beginning for ancestral rites.
The Saurapurāṇa is cited jointly with the Śivarahasya for the tithi-beginning/end rule distinguishing divine and ancestral rites.
The Māradoyapurāṇa is cited for two verses on the divine-end / ancestral-beginning tithi rule and the significance of sunset in ancestral rites.
The Skanda Purāṇa is cited twice: once for the binary forenoon/afternoon definition and once for the five-muhūrta fivefold division of the day.
The Vāyu Purāṇa is cited for the verse defining the kutapa as the time between the seventh and ninth muhūrta.
The Kālikā Purāṇa is cited for the verse listing nine 'ku-tāpas' (destroyers of sin) including Brahmin, blanket, cows, silver, fire, guests, sesame, Darbha grass, and midday.
The Prabhāsakhaṇḍa is cited twice: once for the eight kutapas including midday and rhinoceros-horn vessel, and once for the rule that muhūrtas are always fifteen in number.
The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the verse specifying the timing sequence of the four types of śrāddha: daivika in the forenoon, pārvaṇa in the afternoon, ekoddiṣṭa at midday, vṛddhi in the morning.

The Matsya Purāṇa is cited three times: for the evening prohibition on śrāddha, for the kutapa as the eighth muhūrta commencing the pārvaṇa, and for the saṅkrānti piṇḍa-prohibition verse debated by Vācaspati.

citations.quote: The *Śatapatha śruti* indicates a fivefold division: "The sun is indeed all the seasons. When it rises, it is spring..."
citations.justification: The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa is cited as Vedic śruti authority for the fivefold seasonal analogy of the day's five parts.

citations.quote: From this verse cited by Mādhava in the *Śivarāghavasaṃvāda*
citations.justification: The Śivarāghavasaṃvāda is cited via Mādhava for the verse prohibiting morning śrāddha outside of vṛddhi occasions.
The Devī Purāṇa is cited for the rule that an eldest daughter should avoid the piṇḍa-offering during the Trayodaśī-Maghā śrāddha worship.

citations.cited_work: Brahma Purāṇa (second citation in piṇḍa section)
citations.quote: In the *Brahma Purāṇa*, having read the verse of the *Matsya Purāṇa*
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited again in the piṇḍa-prohibition section as a text that reads and thereby endorses the Matsya Purāṇa verse on learned Brahmins visiting the house.

citations.quote: the verse of the *Brahmavaivarta* cited by Hemādri
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa is cited via Hemādri for the verse restricting piṇḍa-offering in the Gaṅgā during Capricorn eclipse, which the Vīramitrodaya limits in scope.
The Smṛtiratnāvalī is cited for the verse enjoining śrāddha effort at son-birth, Vyatīpāta, and eclipses while prohibiting piṇḍa-offering.
The Prayogapārijāta is cited as the source of a list of inauspicious times (Nandā, Aśvinī, Kāma, Sunday, Tuesday, etc.) for piṇḍa-offering in the Mahālaya dark fortnight.

citations.quote: since in the *Hemādri*, a *śrāddha* is enjoined on a *tithi* and a day of the week
citations.justification: Hemādri's digest is cited and extended to argue that piṇḍa prohibitions tied to a tithi or weekday apply only to śrāddhas occasioned by those, not to general śrāddhas.

citations.quote: the sūtra of Āpastamba, "Or in a commenced rite, the connection is until the completion"
citations.justification: The Āpastamba Dharmasūtra is cited as the sūtra-level authority supporting the view that a commenced śrāddha may be completed beyond the primary time.
